nodes.Name: item
nodes.DocComment: item represents a token or text string returned from the scanner.

Fields.Name: pos
Fields.DocComment: The starting position, in bytes, of this item in the input string.

Fields.Name: line
Fields.DocComment: The line number at the start of this item.

nodes.Name: itemType
nodes.DocComment: itemType identifies the type of lex items.

nodes.Name: key
nodes.ValueLiteral: map[string]itemType{".": itemDot, "block": itemBlock, "break": itemBreak, "continue": itemContinue, "define": itemDefine, "else": itemElse, "end": itemEnd, "if": itemIf, "range": itemRange, "nil": itemNil, "template": itemTemplate, "with": itemWith}

nodes.Name: spaceChars
nodes.DocComment:
Trimming spaces.
If the action begins "{{- " rather than "{{", then all space/tab/newlines
preceding the action are trimmed; conversely if it ends " -}}" the
leading spaces are trimmed. This is done entirely in the lexer; the
parser never sees it happen. We require an ASCII space (' ', \t, \r, \n)
to be present to avoid ambiguity with things like "{{-3}}". It reads
better with the space present anyway. For simplicity, only ASCII
does the job.

nodes.Name: stateFn
nodes.DocComment: stateFn represents the state of the scanner as a function that returns the next state.

nodes.Name: lexer
nodes.DocComment: lexer holds the state of the scanner.

Fields.Name: name
Fields.DocComment: the name of the input; used only for error reports

Fields.Name: atEOF
Fields.DocComment: we have hit the end of input and returned eof

nodes.Name: lexOptions
nodes.DocComment: lexOptions control behavior of the lexer. All default to false.

nodes.Name: next
nodes.DocComment: next returns the next rune in the input.

nodes.Name: peek
nodes.DocComment: peek returns but does not consume the next rune in the input.

nodes.Name: backup
nodes.DocComment: backup steps back one rune.

nodes.Name: thisItem
nodes.DocComment:
thisItem returns the item at the current input point with the specified type
and advances the input.

nodes.Name: emit
nodes.DocComment: emit passes the trailing text as an item back to the parser.

nodes.Name: emitItem
nodes.DocComment: emitItem passes the specified item to the parser.

nodes.Name: ignore
nodes.DocComment:
ignore skips over the pending input before this point.
It tracks newlines in the ignored text, so use it only
for text that is skipped without calling l.next.

nodes.Name: accept
nodes.DocComment: accept consumes the next rune if it's from the valid set.

nodes.Name: acceptRun
nodes.DocComment: acceptRun consumes a run of runes from the valid set.

nodes.Name: errorf
nodes.DocComment:
errorf returns an error token and terminates the scan by passing
back a nil pointer that will be the next state, terminating l.nextItem.

nodes.Name: nextItem
nodes.DocComment:
nextItem returns the next item from the input.
Called by the parser, not in the lexing goroutine.

nodes.Name: lex
nodes.DocComment: lex creates a new scanner for the input string.

nodes.Name: lexText
nodes.DocComment: lexText scans until an opening action delimiter, "{{".

nodes.Name: rightTrimLength
nodes.DocComment: rightTrimLength returns the length of the spaces at the end of the string.

nodes.Name: atRightDelim
nodes.DocComment: atRightDelim reports whether the lexer is at a right delimiter, possibly preceded by a trim marker.

nodes.Name: leftTrimLength
nodes.DocComment: leftTrimLength returns the length of the spaces at the beginning of the string.

nodes.Name: lexLeftDelim
nodes.DocComment:
lexLeftDelim scans the left delimiter, which is known to be present, possibly with a trim marker.
(The text to be trimmed has already been emitted.)

nodes.Name: lexComment
nodes.DocComment: lexComment scans a comment. The left comment marker is known to be present.

nodes.Name: lexRightDelim
nodes.DocComment: lexRightDelim scans the right delimiter, which is known to be present, possibly with a trim marker.

nodes.Name: lexInsideAction
nodes.DocComment: lexInsideAction scans the elements inside action delimiters.

nodes.Name: lexSpace
nodes.DocComment:
lexSpace scans a run of space characters.
We have not consumed the first space, which is known to be present.
Take care if there is a trim-marked right delimiter, which starts with a space.

nodes.Name: lexIdentifier
nodes.DocComment: lexIdentifier scans an alphanumeric.

nodes.Name: lexField
nodes.DocComment:
lexField scans a field: .Alphanumeric.
The . has been scanned.

nodes.Name: lexVariable
nodes.DocComment:
lexVariable scans a Variable: $Alphanumeric.
The $ has been scanned.

nodes.Name: lexFieldOrVariable
nodes.DocComment:
lexFieldOrVariable scans a field or variable: [.$]Alphanumeric.
The . or $ has been scanned.

nodes.Name: atTerminator
nodes.DocComment:
atTerminator reports whether the input is at valid termination character to
appear after an identifier. Breaks .X.Y into two pieces. Also catches cases
like "$x+2" not being acceptable without a space, in case we decide one
day to implement arithmetic.

nodes.Name: lexChar
nodes.DocComment:
lexChar scans a character constant. The initial quote is already
scanned. Syntax checking is done by the parser.

nodes.Name: lexNumber
nodes.DocComment:
lexNumber scans a number: decimal, octal, hex, float, or imaginary. This
isn't a perfect number scanner - for instance it accepts "." and "0x0.2"
and "089" - but when it's wrong the input is invalid and the parser (via
strconv) will notice.

nodes.Name: lexQuote
nodes.DocComment: lexQuote scans a quoted string.

nodes.Name: lexRawQuote
nodes.DocComment: lexRawQuote scans a raw quoted string.

nodes.Name: isSpace
nodes.DocComment: isSpace reports whether r is a space character.

nodes.Name: isAlphaNumeric
nodes.DocComment: isAlphaNumeric reports whether r is an alphabetic, digit, or underscore.
